scope: Private native Linux fresh-page bootstrap diagnostics; no suite-level speed or final acceptance claim.

plan.change: Dispatch five initial domain commands in their existing order before awaiting their replies in that order. Existing native target/session ownership, all following setup order, closure and publication gates remain. Private env switch, default off. No native browser changes.
plan.diagnostic: Four 15-context API runs with reversed off/on order; cumulative bootstrap stage audit and warm API intervals. Diagnostic logging enabled equally; not suite performance.
plan.advancement: Proceed to original-runner controls and complete-suite comparison only if warm page-create median improves at least 20% in both orders and focused newPage lifecycle controls pass. Otherwise retain attribution and restore baseline; this threshold selects investigation only.
plan.custody: Command handles remain owned in a vector until their original replies settle or the original-page cleanup path runs. Dispatched commands can outlive a dropped handle; page disposal, not reply drainage, owns failure cleanup.

decision.reason: Warm page creation improves 19.800745% and 20.756342%; the prospective >=20% in both orders threshold fails. Domain interval drops about 1ms in both orders. Preserve useful measured component savings without claiming whole-suite benefit.
decision.nextQuestion: Separately attribute fixed runner/owner time versus per-test cost at different suite sizes, preserving all nine original acceptance scenarios. Do not repeat this unchanged domain-only screen or redefine acceptance around larger easier cases.

restoration.note: Candidate executable preserved separately; source and known baseline executable restored. Target-directory intermediate objects are candidate objects until the next rebuild.

limitations: Warm medians include audit logging and compare two runs per mode, not confidence-qualified complete suites.
Five-command dispatch order is retained; cancellation may drop replies after native dispatch. Original-page disposal owns failure cleanup.

This result does not bound a coarse native bootstrap transaction or establish broader compatibility/resource acceptance.
